newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 2.7 million barrels Aug LSWR.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 2.7 million barrels Aug LSWR.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina has allocated a total of 2.7 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for August lifting, industry sources said on Tuesday.
The allocation compared with the initial allocation of 2.3 million barrels in July, with additional 300,000 barrels rolled over from June.
Pertamina allocated 3.1 million barrels in June with 500,000 barrels rolled over from May.
The comparitively small July and August allocations were due to a shutdown of some units at its 200,000 barrel-per-day Balikpapan refinery for maintenance from July 10 for 32 days, traders said.
"But when Balikpapan restarts in mid-August, Indonesia should allocate more LSWR. Supplies in August won't be as tight as in July," said one trader.
Another trader said he did not see significant demand from Japan and assessed LSWR prices at between $16.00 and $16.50 per barrel in the near term, free on board Singapore.
